VERSANT
A POWER
Testimony in Neither for Nor Against LD 873 An Act to Expand Municipal Authority over Utility Pole Permits
March 18, 2025
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and members of the committee, my name is James Cote and I am here on behalf of Versant Power neither for nor against LD 873.
Current law allows municipal officers of a municipality with more than 40,000 residents, after notice and hearing, to revoke the location of a utility pole in a public way for public safety and welfare. Currently,
only Portland is eligible for this authority.
LD 873 would reduce the municipal threshold from 40,000 to 30,000 residents, providing this authority
to the cities of Lewiston and Bangor, in addition to Portland. We would like to highlight that Versant
believes its relationship with the City of Bangor is a very positive one, and that we proactively work with
them on problematic pole locations periodically. Versant has not been made aware of any issues that would require a change in statute.
We believe that if a solution can be reached without a statutory change than maintaining current
statutory requirements provides the most predictability for all parties and reduces the potential of customers shouldering the costs for unnecessary pole relocation work.
We would be happy to participate in a discussion with the PUC and relevant stakeholders should the
committee ask us to do so.
Thank you for your consideration and we would be pleased to provide any supplemental information for
the work session.

Testimony in Neitherfor Nor Against LD 873
An Act to Expand Municipal Authority over Utility Pole Permits
March 18, 2025
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and members of the committee, my name is James Cote and I am here on behalf of Consolidated Communications neither for nor against LD 873.
Current law allows municipal officers of a municipality with more than 40,000 residents, after
notice and hearing, to revoke the location of a utility pole in a public way for public safety and
welfare. Currently, only Portland is eligible for this authority.
LD 873 would reduce the municipal threshold from 40,000 to 30,000 residents, providing this authority to the cities of Lewiston and Bangor, in addition to Portland.
Our position truly stems from a lack of understanding about what the bill seeks to achieve and
concern for unintended consequences. We have not been made aware of any issues that would
require a change in statute.
Being directed to move the location of existing poles could potentially cause unintended
consequences. For example, if a municipality of this size were to require the relocation of a pole away from the street to the backside of a sidewalk it could place utility lines in close and unsafe proximity to residential and commercial buildings. Without appropriate training and education it would be difficult for municipalities to make these determinations without conversations with pole owners.
Additionally, requiring that poles be removed and relocated can sometimes be costly to customers and disruptive to residents of the municipality.
In light of these concerns, and our lack of awareness of current municipal concerns, we would
urge the committee to instead direct the pole owners, concerned municipal stakeholders, and the Public Utilities Commission to have a discussion about what the objective of this legislation is and whether or not it can be resolved without statutory change. Consolidated Communications would be pleased to participate in that discussion. If no resolution can be agreed upon, the committee
could then deliberate on appropriate amendments to existing statute and rule to accommodate
any necessary changes. We believe that if a solution can be reached without statutory change
than maintaining current statutory requirements provides the most predictability for all parties.
Thank you for your consideration and we would be pleased to provide any supplemental
information for the work session.

Testimony on behalf of Central Maine Power Company Neither For Nor Against LD 873: An Act to Expand Municipal Authority Over Utility Pole Permits
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology, my name is Kathleen Newman, Vice President of Government Affairs for Central Maine Power Company, submitting testimony neither for nor against LD 873: An Act to Expand Municipal Authority Over Utility Pole Permits.
The City of Lewiston is a CCI pole-set area which means CMP and CCI jointly own the poles and CCI is
responsible for maintenance though we work closely together to resolve any issues that come up.
We understand this legislation stems from a situation on Holland Street that resulted when sidewalks
were updated following a construction project that left poles, with attachments and conduit (and a fire hydrant) in the sidewalk. See before and after photos below:

Pole l5 (before)

Pole l5 (after)

In this particular instance we were not approached to address the situation. However, since identifying
it, our local sen/ice center manager has been in touch with the city to work on a solution. While the pole
placement is ADA compliant (36" of clearance on the sidewalk), the attachments are impeding the
sidewalk. This morning he discussed a plan with the City to relocate the communications box and
conduits pictured above.

Our team also identified another pole on Holland Street that is
marginal with respect to ADA compliance (see picture, right). We'll work with CCl and the city to address ADA compliance for
this pole as well.
ln speaking to multiple city officials we've learned this situation
was not a problem with responsiveness from CMP -- we were not
approached to move our facilities -- but rather a concern about
addressing the ADA compliance post-construction and the cost
of doing so.
We do not believe it is necessary to amend the statute that
allows municipal officials of Maine's largest cities to order poles removed to address public safety and public welfare concerns. Particularly as this statute would require the city to notice and hold a public hearing for such determination.
We're happy to work with with any municipality, of any size, to address ADA compliance concerns
Thank you for your consideration.

Testimony ofRepresentative Mana Abdi presenting
LD 873, An Act to Expand Municipal Authority over Utility Pole Permits
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology
Good afternoon Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology. My name is Mana Abdi, and I represent House District 95, which includes a portion of Lewiston. I am here today to introduce LD 873, An
Act to Expand Municipal Authority Over Utility Pole Permits.
This bill was brought to my attention by a member of our city council. Under current law, only
municipalities with populations exceeding 40,000 have the authority to revoke the location of a
utility pole when required for public safety and welfare. This bill seeks to extend that authorization
to municipalities with at least 30,000 residents.
Modifying the language here to permit a community of 35,000 inhabitants, for instance, includes Lewiston in granting the ability to address and correct infrastructure issues in the form of pole
location placement when and if the problem arises via the municipal process. Cmrently, under
Lewiston ordinance, we only have that power when there is a new highway and sidewalk project, at
l
least from my reading, and it seems to clash with the above state guidance.
The City of Lewiston has consistently raised concerns about the timely relocation of above-ground
utilities. Many residents rely on bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure for their daily commutes,
including travel to work and school. Unfortunately, transitioning utilities from old poles can take years, leaving redundant structures that obstruct mobility and potentially violate Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. In winter, these obstructions force pedestrians into the street,
creating hazardous conditions.
Lewiston has entire poles that have been abandoned, protruding into sidewalks and causing long-term safety and accessibility issues. Others, having sustained damage, have been hastily
repaired, posing additional risks. I believe many of the municipalities represented in this room have

District 95: Part of Lewiston

faced similar challenges, and this bill would provide the necessary tools to address them more
efficiently.
I urge the committee to support this measure, as it directly impacts public safety, accessibility and municipal autonomy in addressing infrastructure concerns.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to answer any questions.
10037789:
Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Conditional Support Of LD 873 - An Act to Expand Municipal Authority over Utility Pole Permits
March 18, 2025
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and members of the Energy, Utilities, and Technology Committee, my name is Rebecca Lambert, and I am providing testimony in "conditional" support of LD 873 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) elected 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). For reference, MMA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit member service organization and aims to help provide policy solutions that work for all residents in Maine and the LPC guides the advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
MMA polled the members of LPC for their opinion on this bill, which generated overall support for the proposal as it expands home rule--an authority held dearly by most communities. Due to a locality's intimate knowledge of their communities, they are best positioned to identify poles that are no longer placed in a safe location.
Although most respondents favored LD 873, it is worth noting that this bill would only benefit two additional communities, Lewiston and Bangor. To that point, our members question why limit this authority to municipalities of a certain population size and suggest eliminating the threshold all together.
This bill and the poll results will be discussed with our entire LPC on Thursday, March 20. Should the position change based on those discussions I will submit updated testimony. Thank you for your time and for considering the municipal perspective on this issue.
